message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: SuttaCentral CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  SuttaCentral-CI:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Install Docker
        uses: docker/setup-docker-action@v4

      - name: Build
        run: |
          make prepare-tests
          # docker wait sc-frontend

      # split debug logging into separate steps so that it is in its own sections and easier to read and parse
      - name: Debug log - compose logs
        run: |
          docker compose logs
      - name: Debug log - docker ps
        run: |
          docker ps

      - name: Lint
        run: |
          make lint

      - name: Test
        run: make test-server-ci",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs a single CI job on push and pull_request to main with no matrix and no concurrency control, so repeated pushes to the same branch/PR can leave older runs executing while newer ones start. The P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE pattern (cancel superseded runs) fits: runs represent the same workflow and branch/PR, a newer revision supersedes older checks, and the work is CI (lint + test), not release/deployment. Adding a top-level concurrency group keyed by workflow and ref with cancel-in-progress cancels only stale in-progress runs for the same branch/PR, leaving distinct branches isolated and preserving every build/test step and required check for the latest run. No permissions, secrets, deployment, publishing, or new network access is added.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE"]
}
